recorded.rule: Q2 v2: a giveaway, read from the question's own text alone
recorded.prompt:q-sealed: Answer ONLY from this question's own text: its stem and its options. Use no knowledge of the subject at all; treat every term as a word you have never met. Pick an option only when the wording itself singles it out: it is longer or more specific than the others, it repeats words from the stem, the others carry absolute terms such as 'always' or 'never', the stem's grammar fits it alone, or it restates the stem. A cue decides only when it clearly singles out one option over every other; a weak cue, or one another option shares, decides nothing. Otherwise answer 'none'. Say which cue decided it, or that none did.
recorded.outcome:q-sealed: from the question's text alone, the reader picked none; the key is 'a'
recorded.because:q-sealed: All three options open with 'Every' and have parallel form; a's 'covers all cases' is only a weak link to 'no default branch', so none decided.

recorded.prompt:q-sealed:b: Given this page and this question with its key, does a passage of the page rule out this wrong option? Quote the passage.
recorded.outcome:q-sealed:b: the page rules this option out
recorded.because:q-sealed:b: The page says "when a new permitted type is added, every switch that is no longer exhaustive becomes a compile error", so no switch runs and hands the type to a last case.
recorded.prompt:q-sealed:c: Given this page and this question with its key, does a passage of the page rule out this wrong option? Quote the passage.
recorded.outcome:q-sealed:c: the page rules this option out
recorded.because:q-sealed:c: The page says the non-exhaustive switch "becomes a compile error" ("missing cases are caught at compile time"), not a run-time exception.
